name: Toyota RAV4
respect: The RAV4 Hybrid really does use less fuel. Agree before you pivot.

cards.title: Seven seats
cards.line: Every Outlander seats seven. The RAV4 seats five.
cards.why: True, and it is the cleanest contrast in the segment.

cards.title: 10-year powertrain
cards.line: Our powertrain warranty is 10 years / 160,000 km. Toyota Canada's is 5 years / 100,000 km.
cards.why: Say both numbers. Do not call Toyota's warranty fake.

cards.title: S-AWC standard
cards.line: S-AWC is on every Outlander, with modes you can show them for the rain.
cards.why: Standard beats an AWD conversation that starts with "which package".

cards.title: Plug-in commute
cards.line: If the weekday loop fits, the PHEV can do it on electricity. A RAV4 Hybrid cannot plug in.
cards.why: Only if they can plug in. You already have that from discovery.

cards.title: We burn less
cards.line: Tell them the gas Outlander beats the RAV4 Hybrid on fuel.
cards.why: It does not. Gas Outlander is 8.7 combined. Do not die on this hill.

cards.title: Better resale
cards.line: Promise the Outlander will be worth more than a RAV4 in three years.
cards.why: You cannot promise the auction. Compare warranty and payment instead.

name: Honda CR-V
respect: The CR-V Hybrid is efficient and Honda's reliability reputation is earned. Do not sneer.

cards.title: Third row
cards.line: Seven seats standard versus five in the CR-V.
cards.why: This is why families cross the lot.

cards.title: Longer powertrain
cards.line: 10 years / 160,000 km powertrain versus Honda's 5 years / 100,000 km.
cards.why: Accurate Canadian comparison if you keep basic coverage separate.

cards.title: Modes, not a badge
cards.line: Show Snow or Gravel mode instead of saying AWD is AWD.
cards.why: A demonstration beats a slogan.

cards.title: Real plug
cards.line: Offer the PHEV only if their commute and their plug support it.
cards.why: The CR-V hybrid does not plug in. The PHEV does.

cards.title: Fuel win
cards.line: Claim you use less fuel than the CR-V Hybrid.
cards.why: You will get fact-checked in the parking lot.

cards.title: Honda is unsafe
cards.line: Hint that CR-Vs are a bad idea in the mountains.
cards.why: Insulting a car they already trust ends the conversation.

name: Nissan Rogue
respect: The Rogue is a known five-seat compact. Their three-row is a different vehicle.

cards.title: Seven, not five
cards.line: Outlander seats seven. The Rogue does not. Don't let them blur it with a Pathfinder.
cards.why: Keep the comparison on the vehicle they named.

cards.title: Powertrain years
cards.line: 10-year powertrain versus Nissan's 5-year / 100,000 km coverage.
cards.why: A clean, checkable contrast.

cards.title: Standard S-AWC
cards.line: S-AWC is standard here, not a package you hope is on the unit.
cards.why: Package confusion is where Rogue deals get muddy.

cards.title: Yamaha, say it right
cards.line: Play their song on the Yamaha system and stop talking.
cards.why: A ten-second demo beats a feature list.

cards.title: Nobody trusts Nissan
cards.line: Tell them the Rogue badge is embarrassing.
cards.why: Their friend or their boss may drive one.

cards.title: Ours is not a CVT
cards.line: Claim the Outlander gearbox is a regular automatic.
cards.why: It is a CVT. The warranty is the honest answer.

name: Hyundai Tucson
respect: Hyundai's 5-year / 100,000 km coverage is genuinely strong, and they sell hybrids and a plug-in.

cards.title: Separate the warranties
cards.line: Respect the 5-year comprehensive coverage. Then show the 10-year powertrain.
cards.why: Trashing Hyundai's warranty makes you look unread.

cards.title: Third row they do not have
cards.line: A Tucson plug-in is still five seats. Outlander PHEV keeps seven.
cards.why: The family brief is the opening.

cards.title: Standard S-AWC
cards.line: S-AWC on every Outlander versus an AWD conversation on the Tucson.
cards.why: Make it a demo, not a speech.

cards.title: Their three features
cards.line: Line up only the features they named, on the trims that have them.
cards.why: Feature-count contests reward the louder brochure.

cards.title: Only we plug in
cards.line: Say Mitsubishi is the only plug-in in the conversation.
cards.why: Tucson has a plug-in hybrid. You will get caught.

cards.title: Their toys break
cards.line: Call Hyundai equipment junk.
cards.why: Insults are not a comparison.

name: Mazda CX-5
respect: A lot of people prefer the CX-5's steering. Let them have it.

cards.title: Room for seven
cards.line: CX-5 is five seats. Ask if that is actually enough.
cards.why: Space is the factual gap.

cards.title: A plug they cannot get there
cards.line: No CX-5 plug-in. Offer the PHEV only when the commute fits.
cards.why: Do not pitch a PHEV to someone with nowhere to plug in.

cards.title: 10-year powertrain
cards.line: Mazda does not match a 10-year / 160,000 km powertrain warranty.
cards.why: Keep the claim on our number, which you can show.

cards.title: Weather modes
cards.line: Offer a Snow-mode explanation for the trips they actually take.
cards.why: Tied to their driving, this lands. As a slogan, it does not.

cards.title: We out-handle Mazda
cards.line: Claim the Outlander is the driver's car versus a CX-5.
cards.why: You will lose the test drive and the trust.

cards.title: Mazda is for pretenders
cards.line: Smile at people who care how a car steers.
cards.why: That is the reason they came in. Respect it.

name: Hyundai Kona
respect: Kona can be a gas vehicle or an EV. Ask which one they mean before you pitch.

cards.title: Door price
cards.line: RVR ES FWD starts at $24,998 MSRP, before fees. Ask if that is the budget.
cards.why: Price is the RVR's honest weapon. Do not blur in fees.

cards.title: Heated seats on ES
cards.line: Heated fronts are standard on the RVR ES. Mention them if they feel the cold.
cards.why: A base-trim benefit, not a step-up you have to apologize for.

cards.title: Lock mode
cards.line: AWC gives 2WD, Auto and 4WD Lock. Explain when Lock is for low-speed slush, not the highway.
cards.why: Teaching the button is the skill.

cards.title: Powertrain length
cards.line: 10-year powertrain versus Hyundai's 5-year / 100,000 km coverage. Give them the 5-year basic, too.
cards.why: Balanced warranty talk survives a spouse who did the reading.

cards.title: We are the EV
cards.line: Compare an RVR's fuel to a Kona Electric as if they are the same kind of car.
cards.why: If they want an EV, the RVR is not one. Say so.

cards.title: Bring the kids' row
cards.line: Talk about Outlander third-row space while standing at a Kona alternative.
cards.why: Wrong vehicle. You sound lost.

name: Honda HR-V
respect: The HR-V is a tidy five-seat Honda. Reliability feelings will come up. Do not flinch.

cards.title: Open at the RVR price
cards.line: Start at the RVR ES number and ask what they were quoted on the HR-V, fees included on both.
cards.why: Apples to apples, or not at all.

cards.title: 4WD Lock
cards.line: Show 4WD Lock for a slushy lot. HR-V AWD does not give them that button.
cards.why: A specific system difference, not "ours is better AWD".

cards.title: Heat at the base
cards.line: Heated seats on the ES. Confirm the HR-V trim they priced before you claim a win.
cards.why: You told them to confirm. That is the skill.

cards.title: Know when to walk
cards.line: If they want turbo torque and S-AWC, walk them to the Eclipse Cross instead of stretching the RVR.
cards.why: Changing vehicles is product knowledge.

cards.title: RVR is the turbo
cards.line: Tell them the RVR ES is a turbo.
cards.why: It is a 2.0L. The turbo is the Eclipse Cross and the gas Outlander.

cards.title: Honda is unsafe
cards.line: Imply Honda safety equipment is a toy.
cards.why: Honda Sensing is real. Do not sneer.

name: Toyota Corolla Cross
respect: The hybrid version is thrifty. Toyota resale will be their second sentence.

cards.title: Low-rpm torque
cards.line: Eclipse Cross makes 184 lb-ft from 2,000 rpm. Offer the on-ramp, not a horsepower shout.
cards.why: Let them feel the merge.

cards.title: S-AWC on all trims
cards.line: Every Eclipse Cross has S-AWC. Say that, then ask if they actually want it.
cards.why: Standard is only a benefit if their driving needs it.

cards.title: 10 versus 5
cards.line: 10-year / 160,000 km powertrain versus Toyota's 5-year / 100,000 km.
cards.why: The resale conversation can sit beside a warranty you can point at.

cards.title: Have a second car ready
cards.line: If the Eclipse Cross payment scares them, the RVR is the price path. Do not force the turbo.
cards.why: A planned step-down beats a lost customer.

cards.title: We sip less
cards.line: Claim the Eclipse Cross uses less fuel than the Corolla Cross Hybrid.
cards.why: 9.3 combined will not beat that hybrid. Agree and move.

cards.title: We win resale
cards.line: Promise stronger resale than Toyota.
cards.why: Do not promise the future market.
